subproblem.title: Choice of the filling constant: mass and radius estimates for the isoperimetric filling (n = m + 2)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 1, 5(a) and 5(b) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2 (3)–(4), corrected), for n = m + 2 and with the same constants. The number t below is the parent's η₀ω_n, and a = t^{1/n} is the parent's a.

Notation: p := (m : ℝ) + 1 > 0, which is also the cast of the natural number m + 1. n := ((m + 1 + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = p + 1 > 0 (push_cast). Hence (n − 1)/n = p/n, 1/p + 1 = n/p, (p/n)·(n/p) = 1, (1/n)·(n/p) = 1/p, n·(p/n) = p, and 1/(m+1) = 1/p = ((m+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹. All powers with real exponents are Real.rpow.

1. (Constants; parent Step 1.) c ≥ 1 gives c > 0. Put K₀ := c·(2c)^{1/p}·(2n)^{n/p}; K₀ > 0 because every factor is positive. Put t := min{1/(2K₀)^{m+1}, 1/(4cn)}, where (2K₀)^{m+1} is a natural power; t > 0 as the minimum of two positive numbers. Put a := t^{1/n}; a > 0 (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos). Since 1/n = ((m+2 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹, m + 2 ≠ 0 and t ≥ 0, Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow gives a^{m+2} = t.

2. (Properties (i) and (ii) of the parent's Step 1.)
(i) t^{1/p} ≤ 1/(2K₀). Indeed 0 ≤ t ≤ 1/(2K₀)^{m+1} = (1/(2K₀))^{m+1} (one_div_pow), and 1/p ≥ 0, so Real.rpow_le_rpow gives t^{1/p} ≤ ((1/(2K₀))^{m+1})^{((m+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹}. The right side equals 1/(2K₀) by Real.pow_rpow_inv_natCast, since 1/(2K₀) ≥ 0 and m + 1 ≠ 0.
(ii) t ≤ 1/(4cn), and 4cn > 0.

3. (Setup.) Fix s, F, M as in the hypotheses. Let b := 2·n·a·F^{p/n}; by (n − 1)/n = p/n this is the right side of the hypothesis on M. Then b ≥ 0 because n, a ≥ 0 and F^{p/n} ≥ 0 (Real.rpow_nonneg), and 0 ≤ M ≤ b.

4. ((A), first rewriting; parent Step 5(a).) Since 2c ≥ 0 and M ≥ 0, Real.mul_rpow gives (2cM)^{1/p} = (2c)^{1/p}·M^{1/p}. Since M ≥ 0 and 1/p + 1 ≠ 0, Real.rpow_add' and Real.rpow_one give M^{n/p} = M^{1/p+1} = M^{1/p}·M^1 = M^{1/p}·M. This also covers M = 0, because Real.rpow_add' needs only M ≥ 0. Hence c·(2cM)^{1/p}·M = c·(2c)^{1/p}·M^{n/p}.

5. ((A), comparison with b.) We have 0 ≤ M ≤ b and n/p ≥ 0, so Real.rpow_le_rpow gives M^{n/p} ≤ b^{n/p}. Multiplying by c·(2c)^{1/p} ≥ 0: c·(2cM)^{1/p}·M ≤ c·(2c)^{1/p}·b^{n/p}.

6. ((A), computing b^{n/p}.) The factors 2n, a and F^{p/n} are nonnegative, so Real.mul_rpow gives b^{n/p} = (2n)^{n/p}·a^{n/p}·(F^{p/n})^{n/p}.
- Since F ≥ 0, Real.rpow_mul gives (F^{p/n})^{n/p} = F^{(p/n)(n/p)} = F^1 = F.
- Since t ≥ 0, Real.rpow_mul gives a^{n/p} = (t^{1/n})^{n/p} = t^{(1/n)(n/p)} = t^{1/p}.
Hence b^{n/p} = (2n)^{n/p}·t^{1/p}·F.

7. ((A), conclusion.) By Steps 5 and 6, c·(2cM)^{1/p}·M ≤ c·(2c)^{1/p}·(2n)^{n/p}·t^{1/p}·F = K₀·t^{1/p}·F. By (i), K₀ > 0 and F ≥ 0, this is ≤ K₀·(1/(2K₀))·F = F/2. Since 1/(m+1) = 1/p, this is (A).

8. ((B), comparison of F; parent Step 5(b).) Since 0 ≤ F ≤ (as)^{m+2} and p/n ≥ 0, Real.rpow_le_rpow gives F^{p/n} ≤ ((as)^{m+2})^{p/n}. Rewrite the natural power as a real power (Real.rpow_natCast) and use as ≥ 0 with Real.rpow_mul:
((as)^{m+2})^{p/n} = (as)^{n·(p/n)} = (as)^{p} = (as)^{m+1}.
The last step uses p = ((m+1 : ℕ) : ℝ) and Real.rpow_natCast again. So F^{p/n} ≤ (as)^{m+1}.

9. ((B), bounding 2cM.) Using M ≤ b, 2c ≥ 0 and 2na ≥ 0 (gcongr):
2cM ≤ 2c·2n·a·F^{p/n} ≤ 2c·2n·a·(as)^{m+1} = 4cn·a^{m+2}·s^{m+1} (ring) = 4cn·t·s^{m+1} (Step 1).
By (ii) and s^{m+1} ≥ 0 this is ≤ 4cn·(1/(4cn))·s^{m+1} = s^{m+1}.

10. ((B), conclusion.) 2cM ≥ 0 and 1/p ≥ 0, so Real.rpow_le_rpow and Step 9 give (2cM)^{1/p} ≤ (s^{m+1})^{1/p}. Write 1/p = ((m+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹; then Real.pow_rpow_inv_natCast (with s ≥ 0 and m + 1 ≠ 0) gives (s^{m+1})^{1/p} = s. Hence (2cM)^{1/(m+1)} ≤ s, which is (B). ∎
proof_key_steps: Set p = m+1, n = m+2 = p+1 and c > 0. Put K₀ := c(2c)^{1/p}(2n)^{n/p} > 0, t := min{1/(2K₀)^{m+1}, 1/(4cn)} > 0 and a := t^{1/n} > 0, so a^{m+2} = t (Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow).

(A): with b = 2naF^{p/n}, c(2cM)^{1/p}M = c(2c)^{1/p}M^{n/p} (mul_rpow, rpow_add') ≤ c(2c)^{1/p}b^{n/p} (rpow_le_rpow). Since b^{n/p} = (2n)^{n/p}t^{1/p}F (mul_rpow, rpow_mul), this equals K₀t^{1/p}F ≤ F/2.

subproblem.title: Positive unit-ball volume and a small scale below the lower-density threshold
subproblem.statement:
For every n ∈ ℕ the following hold, where ω_n := unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue (volume) measure, a value in [0, ∞], of the open unit ball ball(0, 1) of Euclid n = ℝ^n, and w := ω_n.toReal.
(a) w > 0.
(b) Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be any measure on ℝ^P = Euclid P (no finiteness assumption), let x₁ ∈ ℝ^P, and let η₀, δ be real numbers with δ > 0. Suppose liminf_{r→0, r>0} μ(B_r(x₁))/(ω_n r^n) < η₀. Precisely: the liminf along 𝓝[>] 0 of the [0, ∞]-valued function r ↦ μ(ball x₁ r)/(unitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(r^n)) is < ENNReal.ofReal η₀, with ENNReal division. Then there is a real s with 0 < s < δ and μ(B_s(x₁)) < ENNReal.ofReal(η₀ · w · s^n). Here B_s(x₁) = ball x₁ s is the open ball and s^n is a natural power.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < (unitBallVolume n).toReal ∧ ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (x₁ : Euclid P) (η₀ δ : ℝ), 0 < δ → liminf (fun r : ℝ => μ (ball x₁ r) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) < ENNReal.ofReal η₀ → ∃ s : ℝ, 0 < s ∧ s < δ ∧ μ (ball x₁ s) < ENNReal.ofReal (η₀ * (unitBallVolume n).toReal * s ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 0 and 2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2 (2), with the lower density in place of Θ^{*n}), stated for an arbitrary real η₀ and an arbitrary measure μ.

Notation: ω_n := unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : Euclid n) 1) ∈ [0, ∞] and w := ω_n.toReal. For real r, g(r) := μ(ball x₁ r)/(ω_n · ENNReal.ofReal(r^n)) ∈ [0, ∞], using ENNReal division.

1. (ω_n > 0.) By definition (unfold unitBallVolume), ω_n = volume(ball (0 : Euclid n) 1). The volume measure on the finite-dimensional inner product space Euclid n is an additive Haar measure, so it is positive on nonempty open sets (IsOpenPosMeasure). The ball of radius 1 > 0 about 0 is open and contains 0, so ω_n > 0 (measure_ball_pos _ _ one_pos). This also holds for n = 0, where the ball is the whole one-point space.

2. (ω_n < ∞.) Euclid n is a proper metric space and volume is finite on compact sets, so every ball has finite measure (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence ω_n < ∞.

3. (Part (a).) By Steps 1 and 2, ω_n ≠ 0 and ω_n ≠ ∞. So w = ω_n.toReal > 0 (ENNReal.toReal_pos) and ENNReal.ofReal w = ω_n (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). This proves (a).

4. (Part (b): the ratio is frequently small.) Fix P, μ, x₁, η₀ and δ with δ > 0 and liminf_{𝓝[>] 0} g < ENNReal.ofReal η₀. [0, ∞] is a complete linear order, so the coboundedness side condition holds automatically (isBoundedDefault). Then frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt shows that g(r) < ENNReal.ofReal η₀ holds frequently along 𝓝[>] 0.

5. (Choosing s.) Since δ > 0, Ioo 0 δ ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), so 0 < r < δ holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0. A frequently-true property and an eventually-true property hold together for at least one r (Frequently.and_eventually, then Frequently.exists). Call that r s. Then 0 < s < δ and g(s) < ENNReal.ofReal η₀.

6. (Clearing the denominator.) Let D := ω_n · ENNReal.ofReal(s^n).
- D ≠ 0: s > 0 gives s^n > 0 (pow_pos), so ENNReal.ofReal(s^n) > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos), and ω_n > 0 by Step 1 (mul_ne_zero).
- D ≠ ∞: ω_n < ∞ by Step 2 and ENNReal.ofReal(s^n) ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_ne_top).
ENNReal.div_lt_iff (Or.inl (D ≠ 0)) (Or.inl (D ≠ ∞)) turns g(s) < ENNReal.ofReal η₀ into μ(ball x₁ s) < ENNReal.ofReal η₀ · D.

7. (η₀ ≥ 0.) Suppose η₀ < 0. Then ENNReal.ofReal η₀ = 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_of_nonpos), and Step 6 gives μ(ball x₁ s) < 0 · D = 0. No element of [0, ∞] is < 0, so this is impossible. Hence η₀ ≥ 0.

8. (Rewriting the bound.) We have η₀ ≥ 0, w ≥ 0 and s^n ≥ 0. Apply ENNReal.ofReal_mul twice, then ENNReal.ofReal w = ω_n (Step 3), then associativity:
ENNReal.ofReal(η₀ · w · s^n) = ENNReal.ofReal η₀ · ENNReal.ofReal w · ENNReal.ofReal(s^n) = ENNReal.ofReal η₀ · (ω_n · ENNReal.ofReal(s^n)) = ENNReal.ofReal η₀ · D.
By Step 6, μ(ball x₁ s) < ENNReal.ofReal(η₀ · w · s^n), and 0 < s < δ by Step 5. This proves (b). ∎
proof_key_steps: ω_n = volume(ball(0,1)) is positive (a nonempty open set under an additive Haar measure) and finite (a ball in a proper space), so w = ω_n.toReal > 0 and ENNReal.ofReal w = ω_n.
liminf_{𝓝[>]0} g < ofReal η₀ gives g(r) < ofReal η₀ frequently (frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt). Since Ioo 0 δ ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, pick s ∈ (0, δ) with g(s) < ofReal η₀.
The denominator ω_n·ofReal(s^n) is nonzero and finite, so ENNReal.div_lt_iff gives μ(B_s(x₁)) < ofReal η₀·(ω_n·ofReal(s^n)). Moreover η₀ ≥ 0, since otherwise the right side would be 0.
ofReal η₀·(ω_n·ofReal(s^n)) = ofReal(η₀·w·s^n) by ENNReal.ofReal_mul and ofReal w = ω_n.
